answer: Vault occupancy bonding. Each identity must hold a distinct minimum balance in a shared on-chain vault; the kernel enforces one active identity per funded vault slot, and a bridge contract routes any withdrawal through a 90-day delay. Registering N identities requires N separate funded slots, each locked for 90 days, so an attacker's cost scales linearly with N in locked capital plus time, and withdrawing to recycle funds resets the delay, making mass identity churn capital- and latency-bound.
